company.name: Coffee Meets Bagel
company.one_liner: A dating app that sends you one carefully picked match a day.

facts.summary: Three sisters built a dating app that sends each user a small number of curated matches every day, instead of endless swiping.
highlights: Users get a limited number of quality matches each day.
The app makes money when users pay for extra features.
It already has a large and growing number of users.
Big competitors like Match and Tinder dominate dating apps.

real_deal.summary: No deal. Mark Cuban offered $30 million to buy the whole company, and the sisters said no.

outcome.headline: Kept growing on its own into a well-known dating app.
outcome.story: The sisters turned down the offer, raised more money from investors and grew the app to millions of users. It's private; the value here (~$100M) is an estimate, and an early stake would have been diluted by later fundraising.
